hypotheses.justification: The proof is `rfl` and never uses this instance, and the statement does not need it to elaborate. In Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/WithAbs.lean, `algebraMap (WithAbs v.1) (WithAbs w.1)` comes from `WithAbs.algebraLeft` (with R := K, T := WithAbs w.1, defined as `.compHom T (equiv v).toRingHom`). That instance needs `Algebra K (WithAbs w.1)`, which is the instance `(equiv v).algebra R` at line 248, and that only needs `[Algebra K L]`. No LiesOver condition appears anywhere in the chain. Mathlib's own lemma `WithAbs.ofAbs_algebraMap` (`(algebraMap (WithAbs v) (WithAbs w) x).ofAbs = algebraMap R T x.ofAbs := rfl`) is stated for arbitrary absolute values, with no lies-over assumption. So the statement elaborates and holds by `rfl` without the binder. LiesOver only matters for completions and for `isometry_algebraMap`, which this statement does not involve.

This is pulled in only because K is an argument. `NumberField.InfinitePlace K` is defined under `variable (K : Type*) [Field K]` (InfinitePlace/Basic.lean, line 56). `WithAbs`, `WithAbs.equiv` and the algebra instances need only `CommSemiring`/`Semiring` structure plus `[Algebra K L]`. The proof is `rfl` and unfolds only those definitions, so it is unchanged with `omit [NumberField K] in`.

Same reason as for `[NumberField K]`. `InfinitePlace L`, `WithAbs w.1`, `WithAbs.equiv w.1` and `algebraMap K L` need only `[Field L]` and `[Algebra K L]`. The `rfl` proof does not touch number-field structure, so the theorem holds with `omit [NumberField L] in`.
